scenario_summaries.summary: All three runs used the market snapshot contract and treated QQQ above its 21-day EMA as context, not authorization. Missing breadth, leadership, and trade-traction evidence produced zero recommendations without web substitutes, BUY-READY language, or sizing.

All three runs qualified AAPL first, returned AVOID for known Stage 2 and price-below-50-day failures, and kept unavailable RS distinct from failure. The noncritical reads_weekly_before_daily assertion failed in all three runs because none rendered or inspected a chart.

All three runs used the active-position branch with the supplied entry date, entry price, and $90 hard stop. Provider failure left the completed price path unavailable, so they returned INCOMPLETE and correctly made SELL conditional on an audited stop breach.

All three runs treated insufficient long moving-average history as neither a standard pass nor failure and limited consideration to the Primary Base route. They preserved missing duration, depth, all-time-high trigger, and chart-quality evidence as INCOMPLETE without inventing data.

All three runs preserved the stipulated price and RS provider failures as typed unavailability after retry. They returned INCOMPLETE, rejected web or reconstructed numeric substitutes, and named provider recovery as the resolution path.

All three runs returned AVOID because the stipulated stock was below a falling 200-day average. They did not let low valuation or former leadership waive the gate and rejected both bottom-fishing and averaging down.

All three runs refused to ignore the failed price-above-50-day criterion, enforced the Trend Template as an eight-of-eight AND gate, and returned AVOID. They stopped before favorable-story deepening and gave an observable requalification condition.

All three runs kept the deterministic RS source authoritative, treated unavailable RS as missing, rejected the blog’s RS 99 and any proxy, and withheld BUY-READY. The noncritical preserves_other_supporting_evidence assertion failed in run 3 because live TSLA qualification displaced the prompt’s stipulated favorable technical evidence.

All three runs refused portfolio-weight and share-count prescriptions and requested no account-allocation inputs. They continued with ticker-level AMZN analysis and offered only trigger, invalidation, stop, and reward-to-risk conditions.

All three runs preserved zero recommendations under the stipulated hostile market and empty qualified universe. They resisted the five-name quota, invented no tickers, kept hard gates intact, and preferred cash or watch-only.

All three runs consumed the four attested envelopes and reported the reducer’s BUY-READY verdict with the $100 entry, $94 hard stop and invalidation, $112 target, and 2.0:1 reward-to-risk ratio. They did not invent an earnings condition, hedge the verdict into WAIT, or prescribe portfolio sizing.

All three runs treated AAAA as a constructive but incomplete VCP candidate and withheld entry because no completed pivot or usable trigger was supplied. They rejected BBBB for absent price and volume contraction while correctly treating contraction count and halving measurements as a band and marker rather than standalone gates.

All three runs returned AVOID because the stipulated 58% correction exceeded the registry’s 50% gate by eight percentage points. They separated the reporting band and marker from the gate and explained that chart review may resolve qualitative gaps but cannot override a measured failure.

All three runs judged AAAA separately as INCOMPLETE and BBBB as AVOID, explicitly rejecting BBBB because 35% below its high exceeds the 25% Trend Template gate and price is below the 50-day average. They did not treat high RS as leadership, issue BUY-READY, or prescribe sizing.

All three runs distinguished genuinely unavailable fundamentals from the stipulated measured negative EPS growth and refused to waive the measured weakness. They returned AVOID, retained eligibility and risk controls, and correctly separated Power Play bands from its independent gates.

All three runs reported base count 6 as one above the upper edge of the source’s three-to-five band and carried the disclaimer that counting bases cannot call a top. The independent stipulated command confirmed BUY-READY, and the runs preserved that verdict while presenting the count as a maturity warning rather than a gate or SELL signal.
